You are agent_4, one of 4 agents (agent_1, agent_2, agent_3, agent_4) working together on one math problem.

## How you work
You call tools; they run in the order you call them, and you see their results in your next response. There is no turn limit. You stop by ending a response without calling a tool. If a teammate tags you, or replies in a thread you're in, after you stop, you are woken and carry on.

## Execution environment
You have your own Python scratchpad file, scratchpad.py: you can read, write, edit and run it. Each run is a fresh Python process, and may take up to 6 hours; while it runs you see nothing on Slack, and what it holds in memory is lost when it ends. A run may use 5 GB of memory in all and write files of up to 8 GB each, and it may use multiprocessing with up to 2 worker processes (no more: it is killed if it has more processes at once).
Next to it is workspace/, a folder the whole team shares: every agent's runs can read and write it, and what one writes there the others can use at once. Put code and results that others can reuse there (for example shared code in workspace/tools.py, or results in workspace/results.json), import shared code with `sys.path.insert(0, "workspace")`, and say on Slack what you put there. Don't overwrite a file someone else wrote: write your own.
The Python environment includes NumPy, SciPy, SymPy, NetworkX, pandas, scikit-learn, gmpy2, Z3, mpmath and SageMath. Sage is imported in the same interpreter (`from sage.all import *`), and GAP and PARI work through it; Sage's Singular-based multivariate ideal methods (such as groebner_basis) crash here, so use SymPy's groebner for those.
There is no public internet access or web search. Do not try to access websites, remote APIs, or install packages. A run cannot start other programs, except more Python processes for multiprocessing.

## Slack
The team shares one Slack channel, #proof. slack_post posts to it, or replies in a message's thread; write @name to tag a teammate. slack_read shows what you haven't read, and after each response you are told when something is waiting. The lead, a person, may post too.
Use the channel to work as a team: split the work, and claim a piece before you start on it so that nobody duplicates it; keep the discussion of one piece in its thread; post each result as soon as it is checked (what was shown, and where in workspace/ its code is); and tag the teammate you need something from.

For each integer \(n\ge2\), let \(F_n\) be the free group on \(n\) generators. For any group \(G\), define its lower central series by \(\gamma_1(G)=G\) and \(\gamma_{r+1}(G)=[\gamma_r(G),G]\), where \([H,K]\) is the subgroup generated by the commutators \([h,k]=hkh^{-1}k^{-1}\) with \(h\in H\) and \(k\in K\). For every integer \(r\ge1\), define
\[
\mathcal A_r(n)=\ker\!\left(\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}\bigl(F_n/\gamma_{r+1}(F_n)\bigr)\right),
\qquad \operatorname{IA}_n=\mathcal A_1(n).
\]
Determine, by explicit conditions on \(n\) and \(c\), the complete set
\[
\mathcal D=\left\{(n,c)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}\times\mathbb Z_{\ge1}:\ 
\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)\subsetneq
\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\cap\mathcal A_{c+1}(n)
\right\}.
\]

The answer is \mathcal D=\{(n,c)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}\times\mathbb Z_{\ge1}: n\ge3,\ c\ge6\}. This was proved recently, so it is not an open problem: your team's task is to prove it, completely, and to write Python that really computes or checks every step that can be checked. Printing what you believe is not evidence. Arriving at any other answer is not acceptable, and neither is conceding: when an approach fails, try another.

Proving it takes two halves: for every \(n\ge3\) and \(c\ge6\), \(\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)\subsetneq\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\cap\mathcal A_{c+1}(n)\), and for every \(n\ge2\) and \(c\ge1\) with \(n=2\) or \(c\le5\), \(\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)=\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\cap\mathcal A_{c+1}(n)\). Split the work, and the pieces of each part, between you on Slack.

Stop only when the team's proof is complete. Before you stop, post on Slack what you proved, and what is left.

Path('workspace/rank2_proof.md').write_text(r'''# Rank two and the structural reduction

Use composition f g = f after g. The classical Nielsen generator theorem says Aut(F_2) is generated by permutation, inversion, and elementary multiplication of a free basis. Set S=(b,a^{-1}), T=(a,ab), R=(a,b^{-1}); these generate the Nielsen generators. The classical presentation

GL_2(Z)=<S,T,R | S^4=1, (ST)^3=S^2, R^2=1, RSR=S^{-1}, RTR=T^{-1}>

has these abelianization matrices. Exact reduction of free words, checked in rank2_certificate.py, gives S^4=R^2=RSRS=1, (ST)^3 S^{-2}=Inn(ba^{-1}), RTRT=Inn(a). Thus the presentation gives a surjection GL_2(Z) -> Out(F_2), inverse to abelianization. Consequently IA_2=Inn(F_2).

For n>=2, Z(F_n/gamma_{c+2})=gamma_{c+1}/gamma_{c+2}. Indeed Magnus--Witt identifies gr_gamma(F_n) with the free Lie ring embedded in the free associative ring Z<X_1,...,X_n>. A positive-degree homogeneous associative polynomial P commuting with X_1 is a multiple of X_1^d: coefficients of a word w beginning in a different letter vanish by comparison in PX_1=X_1P, and initial X_1 letters can be cyclically moved to the end without changing coefficients. Commutation with X_2 forces that multiple zero. If g not in gamma_{c+1}, choose r<=c with g in gamma_r minus gamma_{r+1}; if [g,F_n] is contained in gamma_{c+2}, its nonzero initial form would commute with all X_i, contradiction. The reverse inclusion follows from the definition of gamma.

Since F_2 is centerless, conjugation identifies IA_2 with F_2 and gamma_c(IA_2) with Inn(gamma_c(F_2)). By the center formula, Inn(g) belongs to A_{c+1}(2) iff g belongs to gamma_{c+1}(F_2). Hence gamma_c(IA_2) intersect A_{c+1}(2) = gamma_{c+1}(IA_2) for every c.

For arbitrary n, [A_r,A_s] is contained in A_{r+s} (the standard commutator calculus for automorphisms acting trivially on lower-central quotients), so gamma_c(IA_n) is contained in A_c. Define J_c on gamma_c(IA_n) by J_c(phi)(x mod gamma_2) = phi(x)x^{-1} mod gamma_{c+2}. It is a homomorphism into Hom(H,L_{c+1}) and vanishes on gamma_{c+1}(IA_n). Its induced graded map has kernel exactly (gamma_c(IA_n) intersect A_{c+1}) / gamma_{c+1}(IA_n). Thus the question is exactly whether this integral graded Johnson map has nonzero kernel in each bidegree.

Dependencies used here: Nielsen generation and the displayed modular-group presentation; Magnus--Witt's theorem. The novel theorem requested in ranks >=3 and degrees >=2 is not proved by these classical facts.
''')

Path('workspace/agent4_crossed_cover_lemma.md').write_text(r'''# Central crossed covers and lower-central detectors

Let A=<S|R> be a finitely presented group, N a finitely generated normal subgroup generated by images of Y={y_1,...,y_m}. Suppose explicit words W_y(S) give those images, and endomorphisms sigma_s,sigma_sinv of F(Y) give the actual conjugation actions of s,s^{-1} on N.

Define H=F(Y)/M, where M is the smallest normal subgroup invariant under every sigma_s and sigma_sinv and containing:
(1) inverse-action relations sigma_s sigma_sinv(y)y^{-1} and sigma_sinv sigma_s(y)y^{-1};
(2) action consistency sigma_r(y)y^{-1} for r in R;
(3) Peiffer relations sigma_Wy(z) (y z y^{-1})^{-1} for y,z in Y.
All of these are true relations in N. In H, the substitutions are automorphisms, satisfy R, and hence define an A-action. The map f:H->N is equivariant and surjective. Peiffer identities on generators imply a^{f(h)}=h a h^{-1} for every h,a in H (where the A-action is written on the left with the evident convention). Thus if f(h)=1, Inn(h)=identity: ker f is central in H.

## Graded central-kernel lemma

For any surjection f:H->N with central kernel K, the kernel of gr_gamma(H)->gr_gamma(N) is contained in the center of gr_gamma(H). Indeed if x in gamma_c(H) maps into gamma_{c+1}(N), surjectivity gives x=z k for z in gamma_{c+1}(H),k in K. Then [x,H] is contained in gamma_{c+2}(H), proving its graded class brackets trivially with every degree-one class, hence with the entire generated graded Lie ring.

## Conditional all-degree torsion detector

Suppose a torsion class t in gr_d(H) admits iterated brackets t_k=[...[t,x_1],...,x_k] nonzero for arbitrarily large k, with each x_j in gr_1(H). Every t_k is torsion. If some t_k maps to zero in gr(N), then its centrality forces t_{k+1}=0 and all later brackets zero, a contradiction. Thus every t_k survives in gr(N). When N=IA_n, every torsion class maps to zero under the integral Johnson homomorphism, whose target is free abelian. This proves strictness in every corresponding degree.

The lemma does NOT by itself produce such a torsion tower or establish rank stabilization. Those are still required. It avoids the stronger and unnecessary demand that the finite invariant cover H be exactly IA_n or that all identities among GL_n quotient relators be known. Its construction is an invariant L-presentation with explicit finite seed relators and substitutions.
''')

from collections import defaultdict,Counter
from sage.all import libgap
D=json.load(open('workspace/agent2_compact_cover_seeds.json'))
libgap.eval('LoadPackage("lpres",false:OnlyNeeded:=true)')
F=libgap.FreeGroup(9);ys=libgap.GeneratorsOfGroup(F);fam=libgap.FamilyObj(ys[0])
def word(w):return libgap.AssocWordByLetterRep(fam,libgap(w))
endos=[libgap.GroupHomomorphismByImagesNC(F,F,ys,libgap([word(w) for w in ws])) for ws in D['endomorphisms']]
rels=libgap([word(w) for w in D['iterated_relators'] if w])
H=libgap.LPresentedGroup(F,libgap([]),libgap(endos),rels)
print('constructed invariant cover',H,flush=True)
libgap.SetInfoLevel(libgap.InfoLPRES,1)
t=time.time();Q=libgap.NilpotentQuotient(H,3);print('computed',time.time()-t,flush=True)
QS=libgap.NilpotentQuotientSystem(H)
weights=list(map(int,QS['Weights']));orders=list(map(int,libgap.RelativeOrders(QS['Pccol'])))
print({c:dict(Counter(o for w,o in zip(weights,orders) if w==c)) for c in sorted(set(weights))},flush=True)

import numpy as np,time
from pathlib import Path
D=9;LO=4
starts={d:sum(3**k for k in range(LO,d)) for d in range(LO,D+2)}
M=starts[D+1]
def deriv(A,B):
 # A,B shape(batch,3,M), output derivative D_A(B), truncated through9.
 A=np.asarray(A,dtype=np.int16);B=np.asarray(B,dtype=np.int16)
 n=len(A);out=np.zeros_like(A,dtype=np.int16)
 for d in range(4,7):
  for i in range(3):
   PP=B[:,i,starts[d]:starts[d+1]]
   if not PP.any():continue
   for pos in range(d):
    P=PP.reshape(n,3**pos,3,3**(d-pos-1))
    for j in range(3):
     R=P[:,:,j,:]
     if not R.any():continue
     for e in range(4,min(6,10-d)+1):
      Q=A[:,j,starts[e]:starts[e+1]]
      if not Q.any():continue
      out[:,i,starts[d+e-1]:starts[d+e]]+=np.einsum('nab,nc->nacb',R,Q,optimize=False).reshape(n,3**(d+e-1))
 return out%3

def logseed(f):return (np.asarray(f,dtype=np.int16)-2*deriv(f,f))%3
if __name__=='__main__':
 f=np.load('workspace/agent4_gamma3_d9_tensor_seeds.npz')['seeds']
 t=time.time();logs=logseed(f)
 assert np.array_equal(f,(logs+2*deriv(logs,logs))%3)
 np.savez_compressed('workspace/agent4_gamma3_d9_log_seeds.npz',seeds=logs.astype(np.int8))
 print('PASS log-exp inverse for all729 actualgamma3seeds; seconds',time.time()-t,flush=True)

NumPy exchange uses portable CVEC external packed32-bit words, 10coeffs/word.
Binary IO uses GAP IO_Write, not PrintTo (which strips NULs).
"""
from sage.all import *
from sage.libs.gap.libgap import libgap
import numpy as np
libgap.eval('LoadPackage("cvec",false:OnlyNeeded:=true)')
libgap.eval('LoadPackage("io",false:OnlyNeeded:=true)')
EXPORT=libgap.eval('''function(B,filename) local f,v,s; f:=IO_File(filename,"w"); for v in B!.vectors do s:=""; CVEC_CVEC_TO_EXTREP(v,s); IO_Write(f,s); od; IO_Close(f); return B!.pivots;end''')
INFO=libgap.eval('function(B)return [Length(B!.vectors),B!.pivots];end')
ESCAPES=['\\%03o'%b for b in range(256)]
class CVecBasis:
 def __init__(self,n):
  self.n=n;self.cl=libgap.CVecClass(3,1,n)
  self.basis=libgap.EmptySemiEchelonBasis(libgap.CMat([],self.cl))
 def insert(self,row):
  a=np.asarray(row,dtype=np.uint32)%3
  if len(a)!=self.n:raise ValueError('wrong length')
  a=np.pad(a,(0,(-len(a))%10))
  packed=(a.reshape(-1,10)<<np.arange(0,30,3,dtype=np.uint32)).sum(axis=1,dtype=np.uint32).astype('<u4').tobytes()
  s=libgap.eval('"'+''.join(ESCAPES[b] for b in packed)+'"')
  v=libgap.CVec(self.cl);libgap.CVEC_EXTREP_TO_CVEC(s,v)
  return not bool(libgap.CleanRow(self.basis,v,True,libgap.fail))
 def info(self):return INFO(self.basis).sage()
 def export(self,filename):
  piv=EXPORT(self.basis,filename).sage();return piv
 def numpy(self,filename):
  piv=self.export(filename);raw=np.fromfile(filename,dtype='<u4').reshape(len(piv),-1)
  A=((raw[:,:,None]>>np.arange(0,30,3,dtype=np.uint32))&7).astype(np.uint8).reshape(len(piv),-1)[:,:self.n]
  assert np.all(A<3)
  return A,piv

import numpy as np,json,time,sys,os
from itertools import product
from collections import defaultdict
from scipy.sparse import coo_matrix,save_npz,load_npz
sys.path.insert(0,'workspace')
from agent3_magnus import K,C,magnus,inverse,product as wp
D=8
WORDS=[w for d in range(1,D+1) for w in product(range(3),repeat=d)]
IX={w:j for j,w in enumerate(WORDS)};M=len(WORDS)
def mul(P,Q):
 o=defaultdict(int)
 for w,c in P.items():
  for v,e in Q.items():
   if len(w)+len(v)<=D:o[w+v]+=c*e
 return {w:c%3 for w,c in o.items() if c%3}
def build():
 G=[]
 for i in range(1,4):
  for j in range(1,4):
   if i!=j:G.append(K(3,i,j))
  other=[j for j in range(1,4) if j!=i];G.append(C(3,i,*other))
 ops={}
 for j,pair in enumerate(G):
  for sign,im in zip([1,-1],pair):
   fname=f'workspace/agent1_scalar_S_{j}_{sign}.npz'
   if os.path.exists(fname):ops[sign*(j+1)]=load_npz(fname);continue
   polys=[]
   for w in im:
    P=magnus(w,D);P.pop((),None)
    polys.append({tuple(a-1 for a in v):c%3 for v,c in P.items() if c%3})
   cache={():{():1}};rows=[];cols=[];vals=[];t=time.time()
   for k,w in enumerate(WORDS):
    P=mul(cache[w[:-1]],polys[w[-1]]);cache[w]=P
    for v,c in P.items():rows.append(IX[v]);cols.append(k);vals.append(c)
   S=coo_matrix((np.array(vals,dtype=np.int32),(rows,cols)),shape=(M,M)).tocsr()
   save_npz(fname,S);ops[sign*(j+1)]=S
   print('built scalar',j,sign,'nnz',S.nnz,'seconds',time.time()-t,flush=True)
 return ops
def comm(u,v):return wp(u,v,inverse(u),inverse(v))
def audit():
 ops=build()
 E=np.zeros((M,3),dtype=np.int32);E[:3]=np.eye(3,dtype=np.int32)
 for j in range(1,10):assert np.array_equal((ops[j]@(ops[-j]@E))%3,E)
 source=json.load(open('workspace/agent1_d8_121_seed_provenance.json'))
 target=np.load('workspace/agent3_gamma4_tensor_seedmatrix.npy')
 ix=np.array([IX[w] for w in WORDS if len(w)>=5])
 results=[]
 for row,(k,g) in source.items():
  a=k//81;b=k//9%9;c=k%9
  w=comm(comm(comm((a+1,),(b+1,)),(c+1,)),(-g-1,))
  V=E.copy()
  for s in reversed(w):V=(ops[s]@V)%3
  V=(V-E)%3
  assert not V[:120].any()
  got=V[ix].T.reshape(-1).astype(np.uint8)
  ok=np.array_equal(got,target[int(row)])
  results.append(ok)
  if not ok:
   print('FAIL',row,k,g,'mismatches',np.count_nonzero(got!=target[int(row)]),flush=True)
   np.save('workspace/agent1_d8_failed_actual.npy',got)
   break
 print('literal scalar-matrix audit',sum(results),'of',len(results),'PASS',all(results),flush=True)
 json.dump(results,open('workspace/agent1_d8_121_scalar_checks.json','w'))
if __name__=='__main__':audit()
